explainer.title: What is vehicle-to-home (V2H)?
explainer.intro: Your EV is already a large battery. Bidirectional charging lets that battery help power your home — not just receive a charge. When the grid is up, you charge as usual. When the grid goes down (and your setup supports it), stored energy can flow back to keep lights, fridge, Wi‑Fi, and other essential circuits running.

compare.normalDesc: Electricity flows one way: grid → your electrical panel → charger → car battery.
compare.v2hDesc: During an outage, compatible systems can reverse the flow: car battery → charger → selected home circuits — safely isolated from the grid.

s1.title: The grid goes down
s1.desc: A storm, utility issue, or rolling blackout cuts power to your neighborhood.

s2.title: The system detects it
s2.desc: A Powershare Gateway or similar transfer equipment senses the outage and disconnects your home from the grid so power cannot backfeed utility lines.

s3.title: Your EV supplies backup power
s3.desc: Energy flows from your plugged-in vehicle through a bidirectional charger to the circuits you planned for backup — often within about a minute, with no generator noise or fumes.

s4.title: Grid returns — charging resumes
s4.desc: When utility power is restored, the system switches back automatically and normal charging continues.

explainer.powershareTitle: Tesla Powershare — how Tesla describes V2H
explainer.powershareBody: Tesla’s Powershare technology is their vehicle-to-home solution. On a fully charged Cybertruck, Tesla states Powershare Home Backup can deliver about 11.5 kW of continuous power — enough for many homes to run essentials for three days or more, depending on what you power and your battery level. Homes without Powerwall typically need a Tesla Universal Wall Connector plus a Powershare Gateway. Homes with Powerwall may use a different path; Tesla continues to expand software and hardware compatibility — we confirm what works for your property on site.

q2.a: We install Tesla Wall Connector setups integrated with Powerwall, and GM Ultium V2H-ready hardware. More brands are added as they become available in our service areas.

q3.q: Do I need Powerwall for V2H?
q3.a: Not always. Requirements vary by brand and vehicle. Tesla V2H often pairs with Powerwall; GM Ultium has its own hardware path. We confirm scope on site.

q4.a: Utility rules vary. We check interconnection requirements during the site evaluation and handle paperwork where required.

q5.q: How is this different from a generator or Powerwall alone?
q5.a: A generator needs fuel and maintenance. A Powerwall is fixed home storage. V2H uses the large battery already in your driveway — you charge it like normal, and tap it when the grid fails. Some homes combine Powerwall plus V2H for longer total backup. We design around your goals and budget.

q1.q: Can one Powerwall back up my whole home?
q1.a: Powerwall 3 is designed so a single unit can provide whole-home backup for many homes. Final scope depends on your loads, panel, and backup priorities — we confirm on site.

q2.q: Do I need solar to get a Powerwall?
q2.a: No. Powerwall works with or without solar. With solar, you store more of what you produce; without it, you can still shift grid energy to lower-cost hours and keep backup power.

q3.q: How is evNation different from a general contractor?
q3.a: We are licensed electricians focused on EV and home energy installs — not handymen. You get code-compliant work, clear communication, and installs built to show off.

q4.q: What happens during a grid outage?
q4.a: Powerwall detects the outage and switches to backup power almost instantly — typically fast enough that electronics stay on without interruption.

q5.q: Do you install other battery brands besides Tesla?
q5.a: Yes. We also install GM Ultium Home Energy, ATG, and Enphase IQ Battery systems. Tesla Powerwall remains our primary recommendation for whole-home backup — we'll help you choose the right fit on site.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have.

s1.heading: 1. Information We Collect
s1.p1: We collect information you provide directly to us, such as your name, phone number, email, home address, vehicle details, and installation preferences when you request an estimate, submit a customer intake form, or contact us.
s1.p2: We may also collect limited technical information automatically, such as browser type and pages visited, to improve our website experience.

s2.heading: 2. How We Use Your Information
s2.p1: We use your information to provide estimates, schedule and complete installations, process financing and rebate applications, communicate with you, and improve our services. We may share information with trusted installation and financing partners solely to fulfill your request.
s2.p2: By providing your phone number, you consent to receive calls and text messages from evNation regarding your inquiry, including via autodialer or automated texting systems. Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies. Consent to receive these communications is not a condition of purchasing any goods or services.

s3.heading: 3. How We Share Information
s3.p1: We do not sell your personal information. We share data only with service partners (such as solar installers, financing providers, and utility rebate programs) as needed to deliver the services you request, or when required by law.

s4.heading: 4. Data Security
s4.p1: We implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect your information. However, no method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

s5.heading: 5. Your Choices
s5.p1: You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information at any time by contacting us. You may also opt out of marketing communications by following the unsubscribe instructions in our emails.
s5.p2: To opt out of text messages, reply "STOP" to any message you receive from us. To opt out of phone calls, notify us directly at GoGreen@evnation.us or 866-913-6199. Opting out of phone or text communications will not affect your ability to receive email updates or request a quote through other means.

s6.heading: 6. Contact Us
s6.p1: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or how we handle your data, contact us at GoGreen@evnation.us or 866-913-6199.
